answer: Memory-hard admission puzzles: each new agent must solve a fresh puzzle seeded at the dawn of the epoch, so work can't be precomputed, and difficulty rises with the tide of signups, so a flood of fakes pays steeply more per identity. Each solution is stamped with a device attestation that acts like a pigment: one rig minting many identities leaves the same tint on all of them, so clusters get flagged and their rewards withheld. Since a fake earns less than the compute it burns, faking doesn't pay.
